title: GRAIL Lands $900M for Early Cancer Detection
summary: GRAIL, Inc. has secured $900 million in Series B funding from a consortium of investors including ARCH Venture Partners, Johnson & Johnson Innovation, Amazon, and others, to advance its early-stage cancer detection initiatives. The funding will support continued product development and large-scale clinical trials, such as the Circulating Cell-free Genome Atlas (CCGA) study, and will also be used to repurchase a portion of Illumina's stake in the company. GRAIL aims to leverage high-intensity sequencing, population-scale clinical studies, and data science to improve cancer biology understanding and provide early detection methods.

title: Best Buy, Target to overhaul stores
summary: Best Buy and Target announced plans to overhaul their operations to compete with Amazon.com, leading to a tumble in their stock prices. These changes, though deemed necessary by analysts, involve costly investments that have made investors cautious, as both companies predict short-term profit pain. Traditional retailers face a "do-or-die moment" as online shopping grows and customer traffic at physical stores dwindles.

title: Coca-Cola Targets Small Retailers With Coke on Demand App
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a "Coke on Demand" app to help small, mom-and-pop retailers easily replenish their stock. The app allows store owners to order products from local distributors, who then use gig workers for delivery, aiming to prevent lost sales and maintain product flow. This initiative targets supply chain "white spaces" and leverages a new delivery model.

title: Amazon Launches Premium Service in Mexico
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has launched its premium service, Amazon Prime, in Mexico, making it the 13th country to offer the service. For an annual fee of 449 pesos (about $23), members will receive free one-day delivery in major cities and two-day delivery elsewhere, as Amazon competes for market share against established companies in the region.

title: Sonos’s Weird-Looking New Speaker Solves A Living Room Design Problem
summary: Sonos has released a new speaker, the Playbase, designed to address the common issue of televisions not being wall-mounted. The 58-millimeter-high device is an oblong, flat shape meant to sit inconspicuously under a TV, offering high-fidelity sound for both music and movies. This release comes as Sonos faces increasing competition from voice-controlled smart speakers and is focusing on integrations with platforms like Amazon's Alexa.

title: Sonos Launches Its First Under-TV Speaker Base
summary: Sonos has launched its first under-TV speaker base, the $699 Playbase, aiming to revitalize the struggling product category with its slim design, easy setup, and integrated multiroom audio. Available April 4th, the Playbase is designed to fit unobtrusively under most modern TVs and offers similar audio performance to the Playbar, differing mainly in its placement and form factor. It includes proprietary audio processing, multiple drivers, and features like Dolby Digital 5.1 decoding, with future firmware updates planned for Amazon Echo voice control integration.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise to Buy Nimble Storage for $1B
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is acquiring Nimble Storage for $1 billion to strengthen its flash storage portfolio and leverage Nimble's customer base and predictive flash technology, InfoSight. Despite Nimble Storage reporting significant revenue growth and new customer acquisition, it has consistently incurred losses. This acquisition is expected to help Nimble achieve profitability faster by integrating it into HPE's larger sales and marketing network and expanding HPE's offerings in the flash storage market.

title: Wal-Mart testing in-store touchscreens in challenge to Amazon
summary: Wal-Mart is testing touchscreen monitors in some Texas stores to help toy shoppers find items or order specific products, as part of its ongoing efforts to compete with Amazon. Wal-Mart CFO Brett Briggs announced the pilot, highlighting the responsiveness and intuitiveness of the new touchscreens, which are intended to bridge the gap between online and physical shopping experiences. This initiative is one of several strategies Wal-Mart is employing, including more self-checkout options and mobile app features, to integrate technology into its retail operations.

title: Wal-Mart's Multiformat Gamble
summary: Wal-Mart is experimenting with new retail formats, specifically "Pickup With Fuel" locations that combine a convenience store, gas station, and click-and-collect service. This strategy aims to compete with Amazon and capture the "last mile" of retailing by offering increased convenience to customers. The article explores Wal-Mart's past attempts at small formats, the details of its new concept, and the challenges and opportunities it presents in the evolving retail landscape.

title: Capital One launches Eno the gender neutral AI assistant
authors: ['REUTERS and STACY LIBERATORE', 'US SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EDITOR']
summary: Capital One has launched Eno, a gender-neutral virtual assistant designed to help customers manage their money through conversational text messaging. Eno is powered by AI and responds as "binary" when asked about its gender, a deliberate choice by Capital One to avoid the criticism often directed at female-voiced digital assistants like Siri and Alexa. The assistant can respond to natural language and emojis, allowing users to check balances or pay bills simply.

title: Juniper Networks Layoffs 2017: Some Staff Cuts Confirmed
summary: Juniper Networks confirmed it has cut a small number of employees as part of a reorganization, attributing the reductions to an "innovation transformation strategy." This figure is significantly lower than initial Business Insider estimates. The company is actively diversifying from traditional hardware sales into software-defined networking and security amidst competitive pressures and shifts to public cloud providers.

title: Corsair Gaming K70 RGB RAPIDFIRE Keyboard Review
summary: This review examines the Corsair K70 RGB RAPIDFIRE mechanical gaming keyboard, highlighting its design, features, and performance. While praising its gaming capabilities and media controls, the review criticizes the sensitivity of the RAPIDFIRE switches for typing, the durability of its plastic components, and the buggy Corsair Utility Engine (CUE) software. The author ultimately suggests the regular K70 or Lux version might be preferable due to the RAPIDFIRE's overly sensitive switches.

title: iRobot Takes Next Step in the Connected Home with Clean Map™ Reports and Amazon Alexa Integration
summary: iRobot announced updates to its HOME App, introducing Clean Map reports that provide visual post-cleaning data for Roomba 900 Series vacuuming robots, detailing cleaning performance and dirtiest areas. Additionally, the app now integrates with Amazon Alexa, allowing users to control their Roomba with voice commands. These enhancements aim to improve the connected home experience by making robot cleaning more user-friendly and informative.

title: Amazon Japan adopts UnionPay to lure Chinese users
summary: Amazon Japan is now accepting UnionPay cards to attract more Chinese shoppers across Asia. This move caters to the growing number of Chinese tourists and online consumers, with Amazon offering reduced shipping rates to China. Other Chinese payment companies like Alipay are also expanding globally to capture this market.

title: Your Next Great Competitor Is... The Odds Favor Amazon.com Over Sears Automotive
summary: This article discusses potential future competitors for independent tire dealers, focusing on Amazon.com, Sears Automotive, and NAPA Auto Parts. It analyzes their current positions and growth potential in the tire sales market, highlighting Amazon's significant online presence and Sears' decline, while NAPA is presented as a sleeper with logistical advantages.

title: Arris Brings ‘RDK-B’ Gateway to Retail
summary: Arris has launched the first retail voice gateway, the SURFboard SVG2482AC, equipped with RDK-B technology and approved for Comcast's network. This device offers a common way to manage home networking functions and will be sold on Amazon and Arris's online store for $249.99, competing with other major DOCSIS modem and gateway providers. The move highlights the growing, albeit small, retail segment of the DOCSIS CPE market.

title: Albertsons reportedly in merger talks with Sprouts Farmers Market
summary: Albertsons Cos. is reportedly in preliminary merger talks with Sprouts Farmers Market Inc., according to Bloomberg. A potential deal would involve taking Sprouts private and integrating the organic grocer into Albertsons' portfolio, enhancing its presence in the natural and organic food sector. This move reflects the ongoing consolidation in the grocery industry as chains confront tight margins and intense competition.

title: Target chooses Kroger exec to revive grocery division
summary: Target has hired Jeff Burt, a veteran executive from Kroger's Fred Meyer division, to lead and revive its struggling grocery business. Burt brings 30 years of experience with Kroger, overseeing multi-department stores similar to Target's model. This strategic hire aims to enhance Target's food and beverage experience amidst fierce competition from Walmart and Amazon.

title: Small Sat Launch Provider Rocket Lab Raises $75 Million to Boost Production
summary: Rocket Lab, a small satellite launch provider, has successfully raised an additional $75 million in funding, bringing its total funding to date to $148 million and valuing the company at over $1 billion. This new capital will be used to significantly increase production of its Electron rocket and meet the high demand from the growing small-satellite industry. The company plans to conduct its first test launches soon and aims for frequent future launches, including up to 19 in 2018.

title: Target Takes Aim at Quick-Trip Convenience
summary: Target Corp. is implementing a comprehensive store redesign, drawing inspiration from Wal-Mart and Amazon, to include "store-within-a-store" convenience sections. This new design features two entrances, one for traditional shopping and another for quick trips, offering grab-and-go items, fresh produce, a Starbucks, and a Wine & Beer Shop. The initiative aims to enhance the shopping experience with time-saving features and expands on Target's plan to open more small-format stores and remodel existing ones.

title: Amazon to buy Middle Eastern online retailer Souq.com: sources
summary: Amazon.com Inc has reportedly agreed in principle to acquire Dubai-based online retailer Souq.com, a major player in the Middle East's e-commerce market. This acquisition gives Amazon a foothold in a rapidly expanding region with a tech-savvy population, although the deal's value is said to be less than Souq.com's previous $1 billion valuation. The move allows Amazon to enter the market without navigating extensive bureaucratic hurdles and capitalize on high demand for Western products.

title: It’s FINALLY official: Amazon is acquiring Souq.com!
summary: Amazon has officially announced its acquisition of SOUQ.com, an e-commerce platform based in the Middle East. This acquisition aims to expand SOUQ.com's growth and bring more products and offerings to customers globally, leveraging Amazon's technology and resources. Both companies emphasize their shared principles of customer-centricity and commitment to long-term thinking to enhance the e-commerce experience in the region.

title: 10 Things You Need To Know About The New DXC Technology
summary: DXC Technology, formed by the merger of CSC and HPE's Enterprise Services, debuted with a focus on digital transformation, talent development, and stable revenue growth. Executives projected first-year revenues between $24 billion and $24.5 billion, outlining strategies for cultural shifts, targeted acquisitions, and organizational streamlining to achieve financial targets. The company aims for significant cost savings and reinvestment to drive a 30-percent return to shareholders by 2020.

title: Amazon buys Middle Eastern online retailer Souq.com, steps up overseas expansion
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has agreed to acquire Dubai-based online retailer Souq.com, signaling a strategic move to expand its e-commerce presence in the Middle East. This acquisition allows Amazon to enter a region where online shopping is gaining traction, beating out a competing bid from Emaar Malls PJSC. The deal comes as Amazon looks for new growth avenues beyond its mature core markets and seeks to compete in emerging e-commerce landscapes.

title: David Einhorn – The Ultimate Shareholder Letter When Your Fund Underperforms
summary: This article highlights David Einhorn's Q4 2015 shareholder letter for Greenlight Capital as a prime example of how to communicate with investors during periods of underperformance. The letter transparently addresses a difficult year, detailing investment losses and comparing the situation to past challenging periods for value investing, while reaffirming Greenlight's investment philosophy and strong team and investor support.
